extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers, architects, art historians, and anyone involved in building or evaluating architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of John Ruskin's The Stones of Venice establishing canons for judging and producing architecture (especially Venetian), combining moral, historical, technical, and presentation principles. The material addresses both lay readers and professional practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Foundations (canons of judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was necessary ... that I should establish some canons of judgment, which the general reader should thoroughly understand, and, if it pleased him, accept, before we took cognizance, together, of any architecture whatsoever. I have called 'the Foundations' the canons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish explicit, comprehensible canons of judgment up front so readers share the evaluative frame; these canons are intended to be generally useful beyond the immediate subject (Venetian architecture). Readers should understand and be able to accept them before evaluating buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal examination and measurement as basis for description
rubrics_metrics.description: My account of every building is based on personal examination and measurement of it... I examined not only every one of the older palaces, stone by stone, but every fragment throughout the city which afforded any clue to the formation of its styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectural description and dating should rest on firsthand inspection and measurement rather than secondary accounts; internal/physical evidence (stone-by-stone, fragments) is the primary source for establishing dates and styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty and avoid overstated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: I am ashamed of the number of times in which I have had to say, in the following pages, 'I am not sure,' and I claim for them no authority, as if they were thoroughly sifted from error...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors/reviewers should candidly state doubt where evidence is insufficient; avoid claiming absolute certainty; separate doubtful estimates from those given as established for main purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intelligibility for the general reader
rubrics_metrics.description: And both in the plates and in the text I have aimed chiefly at clear intelligibility; that any one, however little versed in the subject, might be able to take up the book, and understand what it meant forthwith... the architectural terms necessarily employed (which are very few) are explained as they occur, or in a note... I am especially anxious to rid this essay of ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present architectural criticism and instruction in plain, unambiguous language; explain technical terms in-line or in notes; make essential parts intelligible to even the least learned reader so laypeople can use the knowledge practically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrations and separation of large plates
rubrics_metrics.description: I determined to separate the text and the unreducible plates. I have given, with the principal text, all the illustrations absolutely necessary to the understanding of it, and, in the detached work, such additional text as has special reference to the larger illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all illustrations necessary for comprehension within the principal text; reserve very large, unreducible plates in a detached format. Choose engraving/drawing techniques suited to subjects (line, mezzotint, lithograph, woodcut) even at the cost of uniformity if it better renders architectural character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose methods of proof for clarity and brevity (not only maximal rigor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of proof used in the following essay being only one out of many which were in my choice, adopted because it seemed to me the shortest and simplest, not as being the strongest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer clear, concise lines of argument that can be followed by readers; recognize that alternative, perhaps stronger, proofs may exist, but brevity and understandability are legitimate priorities in exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture principles are universal and practically applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not, indeed, anything in the following essay bearing on the special forms and needs of modern buildings; but the principles it inculcates are universal; and they are illustrated from the remains of a city which should surely be interesting to the men of London...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate principles that apply beyond historical examples; show how surviving examples (Venice) illuminate universal architectural truths useful for contemporary design and lay decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay knowledge and civic responsibility in architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man has, at some time of his life, personal interest in architecture. He has influence on the design of some public building; or he has to buy, or build, or alter his own house... it is intended that all of us should have knowledge, and act upon our knowledge, in matters with which we are daily concerned, and not to be left to the caprice of architects or mercy of contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage civic and domestic actors (owners, purchasers, citizens) to acquire basic architectural understanding so they can make informed decisions and not be subject to bad practice; architecture education is a practical civic duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider architecture as index of civic/moral condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence which I shall be able to deduce from the arts of Venice will be both frequent and irrefragable, that the decline of her political prosperity was exactly coincident with that of domestic and individual religion... the most curious phenomenon in all Venetian history is the vitality of religion in private life, and its deadness in public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge architecture not only on form and construction but as a record of social, political, and moral conditions; architectural forms and ornamentation can indicate broader civic virtues or decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of ornament with structural architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: The wreaths round the columns look as if they would drop off the next moment, and the animals at the bases produce exactly the effect of mice who had got there by accident: one feels them ridiculously diminutive, and utterly useless... The whole building is a most curious illustration of the appointed fate of the Renaissance architects,— to caricature whatever they imitated, and misapply whatever they learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ornament must be properly scaled, positioned, and integrated into the architecture so it appears organic and supportive rather than detached, accidental, or diminutive; avoid applying ornament that contradicts the sense of structural purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inappropriate transplantation of stylistic ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not mean ... to be understood as in the least applying to the detestable ornamentation of the Alhambra. The Alhambra is no more characteristic of Arab work, than Milan Cathedral is of Gothic: it is a late building... The Alhambra ornament has of late been largely used in shop-fronts, to the no small detriment of Regent Street and Oxford Street.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about importing exotic or late-period ornament styles into contexts where they are historically or functionally inappropriate; mechanical repetition of foreign motifs can degrade urban character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and preserve monumental fabric from trivial misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The worst instances I ever saw of sacrilege and brutality were the uses to which the noble base of St. Mark's was put... its purple marbles were, in the winter of 1849, the customary gambling tables of the idle children of Venice... book-stalls and children's toys fastened with twine round the porphyry shafts of the church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect important architectural monuments from being used for mundane or profane commercial purposes; civic guardianship and reverence for historic fabric is a criterion of good stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chamfer construction principles and varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Let B A C, Fig. LXXII, be the original angle of the wall. Inscribe within it a circle, p Q Np, of the size of the bead required, touching A B, A C, in p, p; join p, p, and draw B C parallel to it, touching the circle. Then the lines B C, p p are the limits of the possible chamfers constructed with curves struck either from centre A... There are, of course, an infinite number of chamfers to be struck between B C and p p...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical procedure: construct chamfers by inscribing a circle to determine bead size, derive limits and families of curved and straight chamfers from centers on defined lines; recognize broad typological families (Italian/ southern vs northern chamfers), their geometric generation, and proportional constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varieties and critique of Renaissance bases and shaft treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scuola di San Rocco... fluted pillars are surrounded each by a wreath... capitals are far the richest Renaissance in Venice... But they have all the marked fault of being utterly detached from the architecture... The whole building is a most curious illustration of the appointed fate of the Renaissance architects,— to caricature whatever they imitated...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess Renaissance shaft and base treatment for whether ornament suggests support and relates proportionally to the architecture; be critical of ornament that is finely executed but structurally detached or misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of water in ornament and symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the principal modes of representing water in Greek mythography... the sea in which it rises is symbolized by the dolphins round the head... In the art of the Roman period, the same kind of figurative and symbolic language is employed, but there is a constant tendency to multiply accessories and details... crowded compositions fatigue and distract the eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning symbolic motifs (e.g., water), prefer terse, emphatic representations; avoid over-crowding accessories that dilute symbolic clarity; be aware of historical typologies (river-gods, nymphs, tritons, urns, dolphin motifs) and their differing emphases across periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-copious, decorative crowding in figurative ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: In these crowded compositions the eye is fatigued and distracted by the quantity it has to examine; the language of art becomes more copious but less terse and emphatic...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value restraint and clarity in ornamental program; excessive detail and multiplicity of accessories can reduce legibility and artistic force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture chapter-topics as dimensions of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: (Table of Contents lists dozens of formal elements and topics: The Quarry; The Virtues of Architecture; The Six Divisions of Architecture; The Wall Base; The Wall Veil; The Wall Cornice; The Pier Base; The Shaft; The Capital; The Arch Line; The Arch Masonry; The Arch Load; The Roof; The Roof Cornice; The Buttress; Form of Aperture; Filling of Aperture; Protection of Aperture; Superimposition; The Material of Ornament; Treatment of Ornament; The Angle; The Edge and Fillet; The Roll and Recess; The Base; The Wall Veil and Shaft; The Cornice and Capital; The Archivolt and Aperture; The Vestibule; Foundation of Venice; etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed topics constitute the book's analytic dimensions — discrete elements by which Venetian (and general) architecture is to be examined and judged. Each topic represents a domain of formal, material, and functional criteria to be considered when analyzing or producing architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for dating and style-history (use internal evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every date in question was determinable only by internal evidence, and it became necessary for me to examine not only every one of the older palaces, stone by stone, but every fragment throughout the city which afforded any clue to the formation of its styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish chronological sequence and stylistic development primarily by internal, material evidence in the fabric (masonry, profiles, fragments); be wary of conflicting antiquarian opinions and aim to reconcile by physical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise essential architectural statements over speculative chronology
rubrics_metrics.description: I therefore gave up all thoughts of obtaining a perfectly clear chronological view of the early architecture; but the dates necessary to the main purposes of the book the reader will find well established; and of the evidence brought forward for those of less importance, he is himself to judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on establishing dates and facts that are necessary to the primary arguments; treat more uncertain chronological claims as secondary and leave room for reader judgment rather than making them foundations for broad arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess restorations and interpolations critically
rubrics_metrics.description: By far the greater number present examples of three or four different styles, it may be successive, it may be accidentally associated; and, in many instances, the restorations or additions have gradually replaced the entire structure of the ancient fabric, of which nothing but the name remains...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a building, identify and disentangle successive styles, interpolations, and restorations; recognize that later additions can obscure or falsify the original fabric and must be accounted for in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture should express structural truth and avoid decorative falsification
rubrics_metrics.description: I have spoken... of the way in which the Roman Catholic priests everywhere suffer their churches to be desecrated... The whole building is a most curious illustration of the appointed fate of the Renaissance architects,— to caricature whatever they imitated, and misapply whatever they learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value ornament and form that honestly express structural role and purpose; avoid decorative elements that misrepresent or caricature structural intent (i.e., ornament that pretends to structural function but is merely applied decoration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical presentation choices: engraving/media chosen for fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: For the illustrations of the body of the work itself, I have used any kind of engraving which seemed suited to the subjects—line and mezzotint, on steel, with mixed lithographs and woodcuts, at considerable loss of uniformity in the appearance of the volume, but, I hope, with advantage, in rendering the character of the architecture it describes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select illustration media based on fidelity to subject matter rather than uniformity; accept visual heterogeneity if it better communicates the architectural character under discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical-political appendices as context for architectural judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix entries: Power of the Doges; Serrar del Consiglio; S. Pietro di Castello; Foundation of Venice; Papal Power in Venice; Renaissance Ornaments; Varieties of the Orders; The Northern Energy; Wooden Churches of the North; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectural evaluation should be contextualized by historical and political understanding; appendices of civic institutions, power structures, and wider cultural factors are integral to interpreting architectural form and meaning.
